sources.people_db.dat: scratch/data/people_db.dat (t120 Unicorn engine, decompressed in memory, never written)

basic_people_ca_pa_offsets.note: +48/+50 are the u16s equal to people_db PCAB/PPAB for BOTH type 2 and type 3. The +44/+46 pair named in the task statement is a peak/former-ability pair that coincides only for players sitting at their peak (which is why the three supplied anchors looked consistent). See ptype3_layout_probe / offset votes for the empirical proof.

wire_layout.height_weight_at_body_126: weight_kg, height_cm as SIGNED i16 at body+126/+128: 0 = unset, negative = auto-derived (take abs()); 0/200 random players out of range with abs(), 314/600 without it
wire_layout.ptype3_note: ptype 2 and ptype 3 share the identical WIRE layout (69-byte block always the n==69 read at wire_pos 29, header 5h at body+0, physique at body+126) but different OBJECT offsets (ptype 2 obj_off -0x70, ptype 3 obj_off -0x160) - read from res['reads'], not assumed. Because this decoder reads the wire buffer, one code path is correct for both classes.
